Not syntax validation: rustc keeps a literal as an unchecked token::Lit in the AST (ast::ExprKind::Lit, rust-lang/rust#102944) and reports LitError::IntTooLarge in rustc_ast_lowering (lower_lit -> report_lit_error), after cfg stripping, so `#[cfg(any())] fn f() { 999999999999999999999999999999999999999999; }` builds under rustc. crates/syntax/src/validation.rs runs over every literal of the file, cfg or not, and would reject that program (superset-of-rust). The error belongs where hir-def lowers the literal (hir.rs:275/278 Literal::from, from expr_store lower for exprs and pats): report it there as a body diagnostic and stop the build, instead of lowering 0. That is hir-def lowering, the requesting lane (no-fallback-front-def) or hir-def owner.
